meta.title: Crew parameters for AirOpsEnv's crew model, with public sources
meta.conventions: Each value has sources[] with url, retrieved date and a quote or table reference, and a confidence (high, medium, low). Money is nominal unless a field says 2025 dollars. Nothing here is fitted to JetBlue's or the FAA's decisions.

sources.title: 14 CFR Part 117 (eCFR, versioner API point-in-time 2026-10-01)
sources.ref: Table A to Part 117 - Maximum Flight Time Limits for Unaugmented Operations; § 117.11(a)(1)

sources.title: 14 CFR Part 117 (eCFR, versioner API point-in-time 2026-10-01)
sources.ref: Table B to Part 117 - Flight Duty Period: Unaugmented Operations ('Scheduled time of start (acclimated time)'; 'Maximum flight duty period (hours) for lineholders based on number of flight segments'); § 117.13(a)

sources.title: 14 CFR Part 117 (eCFR, versioner API point-in-time 2026-10-01)
sources.ref: § 117.13(b)(1): 'The maximum flight duty period in Table B of this part is reduced by 30 minutes.'

unacclimated_fdp_reduction.note: Not expected to bind: every JetBlue station in the data lies within 60 degrees of longitude of every base (BOS -71.0 to LAX -118.4 is 47.4 deg), so crews who start the day rested at base stay acclimated (§ 117.3 'Theater').

acclimated_time_reference.value: local time at the point of acclimation, or base time if the home base is in that theater; the certificate holder declares which

sources.title: FAA Order 8900.1 Vol 3 Ch 58 Sec 2 (host unreachable from here; content from search-engine excerpt)
sources.ref: search-engine excerpt: 'may enter Tables B or C using local time at the point of acclimation, or base time if the home base falls within that theater ... the certificate holder will determine and declare whether local or base time will be used'

acclimated_time_reference.note: Used: a pilot flying within the continental US and the Caribbean stays acclimated (one theater), so Table B and Table A read the local time at the duty's report station (a reserve's base, a rest's station).

table_b_inputs_scheduled.value: Table B limit = f(scheduled report time, number of flight segments); the scheduled start cannot change once the FDP begins; adding or cancelling segments after the start changes the limit; a cancelled flight is not a segment; a diversion is not a new segment but its time counts

sources.title: FAA, Clarification of Flight, Duty, and Rest Requirements, 78 FR 14166, 2013-03-05
sources.ref: 78 FR 14171-72, section G: 'The unaugmented FDP limits in Table B are determined using two pieces of information: (1) The time that the FDP is scheduled to begin, and (2) the number of flight segments that will be flown during the FDP. Once an FDP begins, the scheduled time of start cannot be changed ... a certificate holder can change the number of flight segments ... A change in the number of flight segments assigned to a flightcrew member would change the pertinent FDP limit in Table B.'

fdp_starts_at_scheduled_report.value: An FDP begins at its scheduled report time even if the pilot reports late; to move a start, the pilot must be shifted to short-call reserve (RAP starts at the original report) or long-call with notice before rest

sources.title: FAA, Clarification of Flight, Duty, and Rest Requirements, 78 FR 14166, 2013-03-05
sources.ref: 78 FR 14171: 'if an FDP start time is not changed pursuant to the long-call or short-call reserve provisions of Sec. 117.21, then the FDP begins at the time that it was originally scheduled to begin.'

value.who: pilot in command and certificate holder (captain's agreement)

sources.title: 14 CFR Part 117 (eCFR, versioner API point-in-time 2026-10-01)
sources.ref: § 117.19(a)(1): 'The pilot in command and the certificate holder may extend the maximum flight duty period permitted in Tables B or C of this part up to 2 hours. The pilot in command and the certificate holder may also extend the maximum combined flight duty period and reserve availability period limits specified in § 117.21(c)(3) and (4) of this part up to 2 hours.' (a)(2): 'An extension ... of more than 30 minutes may occur only once prior to receiving a rest period described in § 117.25(b).'

sources.title: FAA, Clarification of Flight, Duty, and Rest Requirements, 78 FR 14166, 2013-03-05
sources.ref: 78 FR 14173, section J: 'the distinction between pre- and post-takeoff FDP extensions comes from determining whether the flightcrew member and certificate holder had a reasonable expectation before takeoff that the flight segment would be completed within the pertinent FDP limit ... the flightcrew member ... would be unable to commence a segment that exceeds his FDP limit by over two hours.'

fdp_extension_before_takeoff.note: Captain's agreement assumed (labelled). The >30-min-once rule is moot within one day if crews start the day rested.

fdp_extension_after_takeoff.value: to the extent necessary to land at the next destination or alternate; ends at landing; may exceed § 117.23(c)

sources.title: FAA, Clarification of Flight, Duty, and Rest Requirements, 78 FR 14166, 2013-03-05
sources.ref: 78 FR 14173: 'the post-takeoff FDP extension terminates once the airplane has landed.'

flight_time_after_takeoff.value: Table A may be exceeded after takeoff only to land at the next destination or alternate; before takeoff a pilot who knows he will exceed Table A may not take off

sources.title: FAA, Clarification of Flight, Duty, and Rest Requirements, 78 FR 14166, 2013-03-05
sources.ref: 78 FR 14170: '[i]f a flightcrew member becomes aware, before takeoff, that he or she will exceed the applicable flight-time limit, that flightcrew member may not take off'

sources.title: 14 CFR Part 117 (eCFR, versioner API point-in-time 2026-10-01)
sources.ref: § 117.25(e): 'a rest period of at least 10 consecutive hours immediately before beginning the reserve or flight duty period measured from the time the flightcrew member is released from duty. The 10 hour rest period must provide the flightcrew member with a minimum of 8 uninterrupted hours of sleep opportunity.'

sleep_opportunity_min_h.note: Proposed: hotel transport within the 10 h (no explicit time is sourced); 10 h release-to-report is the binding rule.

rest_after_long_deadhead.value: if deadhead exceeds the Table B FDP, rest = deadhead length, at least 10 h

value.part_of_fdp: only when before a flight segment or between segments without intervening rest

sources.title: 14 CFR Part 117 (eCFR, versioner API point-in-time 2026-10-01)
sources.ref: § 117.3 'Deadhead transportation ... All time spent in deadhead transportation is duty and is not rest. For purposes of determining the maximum flight duty period in Table B of this part, deadhead transportation is not considered a flight segment.' 'Flight duty period ... Examples of tasks that are part of the flight duty period include deadhead transportation ... and airport/standby reserve, if the above tasks occur before a flight segment or between flight segments without an intervening required rest period.'

fdp_definition_end.value: FDP ends when the aircraft is parked after the last flight; duty and rest are measured from release

sources.title: 14 CFR Part 117 (eCFR, versioner API point-in-time 2026-10-01)
sources.ref: § 117.3 'Flight duty period (FDP) ... ends when the aircraft is parked after the last flight and there is no intention for further aircraft movement by the same flightcrew member.'

reserve_airport_standby.value: all time in airport/standby reserve is FDP; it must be designated as such

sources.title: 14 CFR Part 117 (eCFR, versioner API point-in-time 2026-10-01)
sources.ref: § 117.21(b): 'For airport/standby reserve, all time spent in a reserve status is part of the flightcrew member's flight duty period.'; § 117.3 'Airport/standby reserve means a defined duty period during which a flightcrew member is required by a certificate holder to be at an airport for a possible assignment.'

value.rap_plus_fdp_cap_unaugmented: min(Table B limit + 4 h, 16 h), measured from the start of the RAP

sources.title: 14 CFR Part 117 (eCFR, versioner API point-in-time 2026-10-01)
sources.ref: § 117.21(c)(1): 'The reserve availability period may not exceed 14 hours.' (c)(3): 'For an unaugmented operation, the total number of hours a flightcrew member may spend in a flight duty period and a reserve availability period may not exceed the lesser of the maximum applicable flight duty period in Table B of this part plus 4 hours, or 16 hours, as measured from the beginning of the reserve availability period.' (c)(2) and § 117.25(e): rest before a RAP.

sources.title: 14 CFR Part 117 (eCFR, versioner API point-in-time 2026-10-01)
sources.ref: § 117.21(a): 'Unless specifically designated as airport/standby or short-call reserve by the certificate holder, all reserve is considered long-call reserve.'

reserve_long_call.value: notified before the § 117.25 rest; 12-h notice if the FDP runs into the window of circadian low; not usable for a same-day call in a one-day model

sources.title: 14 CFR Part 117 (eCFR, versioner API point-in-time 2026-10-01)
sources.ref: § 117.3 'Long-call reserve'; § 117.21(d)-(e)

cumulative_limits_not_modelled.note: Labelled as not modelled: crews start the day rested.

sources.title: 14 CFR 121.467 (eCFR, point-in-time 2026-10-01)
sources.ref: § 121.467(b)(1): 'no certificate holder ... may assign a flight attendant to a scheduled duty period of more than 14 hours.'

sources.title: 14 CFR 121.467 (eCFR, point-in-time 2026-10-01)
sources.ref: § 121.467(b)(2): 'must be given a scheduled rest period of at least 10 consecutive hours'; (b)(3): 'The rest period required under paragraph (b)(2) of this section may not be reduced to less than 10 consecutive hours.'

sources.title: FAA final rule, Flight Attendant Duty Period Limitations and Rest Requirements, 87 FR 61452, 2022-10-12
sources.ref: 87 FR 61452: 'Effective date: This rule is effective November 14, 2022.' (in force for the whole Dec 2022 - Jul 2026 window)

beyond_control_delay_clause.value: A flight attendant is not scheduled beyond the limit if the flights are scheduled and normally terminate within it but, beyond the carrier's control (e.g. weather), are not expected at departure to arrive within the scheduled time

sources.title: 14 CFR 121.467 (eCFR, point-in-time 2026-10-01)
sources.ref: § 121.467(b)(14): 'A flight attendant is not considered to be scheduled for duty in excess of duty period limitations if the flights to which the flight attendant is assigned are scheduled and normally terminate within the limitations but due to circumstances beyond the control of the certificate holder ... (such as adverse weather conditions) are not at the time of departure expected to reach their destination within the scheduled time.'

sources.title: FAA Office of Chief Counsel, Legal interpretation of 14 CFR 121.467(b)(14), memo dated Aug 16, 2013
sources.ref: FAA memo (Aug 16, 2013): a 13:35 scheduled duty that ran 16:00 after an excused 2:25 delay complied; 'Neither the regulatory text nor the rulemaking history indicates that the certificate holder would be obligated to reassign the flight attendant simply because the excused delay occurred early on in the duty period.' Also: 'The operator's original schedule must therefore be realistic.'

beyond_control_delay_clause.note: Modelling reading (labelled): the 14-h check applies to the duty as scheduled when assigned; any reassignment made on the day must itself be scheduled within 14 h on realistic times.

duty_period_definition.value: from reporting for an assignment involving flight time to release

sources.title: 14 CFR 121.467 (eCFR, point-in-time 2026-10-01)
sources.ref: § 121.467(a) 'Duty period means the period of elapsed time between reporting for an assignment involving flight time and release from that assignment'

transport_not_rest.value: non-local transport to or from an assignment is not rest

augmented_options_not_used.value: 16/18/20-h scheduled duty only with 1/2/3 extra FAs; not used

weekly_24h_off_not_modelled.value: 24 consecutive hours free in any 7 calendar days

part117_option_not_used.value: 121.467(c) lets a carrier apply part 117 to FAs; decision is to use 121.467(b)

sources.title: 14 CFR 121.391 (eCFR, point-in-time 2026-10-01)
sources.ref: § 121.391(a)(3): 'more than 50 but less than 101 passengers - two flight attendants.' (a)(4): 'more than 100 passengers - two flight attendants plus one additional flight attendant for each unit (or part of a unit) of 50 passenger seats above a seating capacity of 100 passengers.' (b): more if the evacuation demonstration used more.
